source.title: Toward Real-Time Edge AI: Model-Agnostic Task-Oriented Communication With Visual Feature Alignment
source.authors: Songjie Xie; Heng-Tao He; Sheng-Hui Song; Jun Zhang; K. Letaief

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether independently trained visual feature spaces can be made usable across models, using learned linear transformations and relative representations rather than measuring convergence with the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the study’s own feature-alignment evaluations and cross-model classification accuracies. The PCA visualizations in Figures 6–7 are described qualitatively, but are not included as rows because the 60-row cap is used for the Table II method-by-condition results and non-alignment controls. Cited results about linear invariance and relative representations are not study results and are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The method rests on linear invariance, but the study's own results show how well one model's features map onto another's. A 16-d linear map fit on 100 anchors restores cross-model accuracy close to the target model's own. That is a direct result on V4, in a new setting: split edge inference over a noisy AWGN channel.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim the methods work across different architectures (Figs 8–10), not only between independent trainings of the same architecture. They state the proposed methods beat fine-tuning by over 10%, but Table II does not always show this (e.g. ResNet SVHN Hyperp: FT 90.59 vs about 94). They note that train/test SNR mismatch remains a gap.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops and evaluates task-oriented visual feature alignment using anchor data, linear transformations, and relative representations; it is not a reproduction of the original representation-similarity measurement method.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by dataset, architecture, alignment estimator, and independent-training variation (WI versus Hyperp). The paper also evaluates SNR settings in figures and notes performance gaps under train-test SNR mismatch.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications
record.problems: The study reports task accuracy rather than a direct quantitative similarity measure between representations. Results concern visual classification on two datasets and a limited set of tailored architectures. Table II provides no uncertainty estimates. The PCA evidence is visual and qualitative.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row cap is reached with Table II’s four alignment approaches and no-alignment controls across architectures, datasets, and training variations. Omitted results include FT comparator values in Table II; PCA visualization findings in Figures 6–7; detailed cross-model pairwise matrices in Figures 8–10; SNR-sweep results in Figures 11–12; and runtime/overhead tables, which do not directly measure interchangeability.

untested.parts: Vision-only classifiers; no language models or paired captions.
Same-architecture different-init pairs exist, but only task accuracy after a map is reported. Shared features, subspaces and unit matching are not measured.
No stitching layers and no mapping without paired anchors. Encoders are tiny (16-d bottleneck), tested only on SVHN and CIFAR-10, and no similarity score is reported.
No neuron, SAE or circuit comparison.
No comparison of metrics or their settings, and no OOD inputs.
No plateau or causal analysis of shared data or objectives.

missing.what: Cross-architecture interchange matrices (6×6 encoder×server) for Non-Align, FT and the three OS estimators at SNR 6 and 18 dB. Off-diagonal aligned accuracy is mostly 84–95%; Non-Align is mostly under 27%.
On-device relative-representation cross-architecture matrices. Off-diagonal CIFAR-10 values go as low as 68.72 and 69.77.
PCA showing independently trained feature spaces differ by rotation and scaling; relative representations look more similar (qualitative).

record.verdict_notes: The study is method-focused but its accuracy-after-mapping results bear directly on V4. Evidence is limited to small split CNNs with a 16-d bottleneck on SVHN and CIFAR-10, with no uncertainty estimates. The record's support label wrongly included the no-alignment control rows.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep; no comparison of alignment as models grow or become more capable.
Only visual image-classification systems are studied; no vision-language models or paired image-caption representations.
The study uses independent trainings, including same-architecture pairs, but does not measure shared features or subspaces across seeds, or compare units or bases.

Tests visual task-oriented communication systems on SVHN and CIFAR-10 using feature alignment; does not test stitching layers, relative representations without paired anchor data, or generality beyond these tasks and systems.
No interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits are compared.
Does not compare representation-similarity metrics or their settings, nor assess out-of-distribution inputs.

Does not test whether shared data or objectives explain alignment, or measure a convergence plateau. It reports cross-model task accuracy after alignment, not completeness of representational convergence.

relationships.condition: Server-based linear maps (LS, MMSE, single-layer MLP) between independently trained same-architecture systems, Table II, SVHN and most CIFAR-10 cells
relationships.reason: Aligned accuracy is within about 0.8–4 points of the original, against 4–23% without alignment (e.g. r02, r22, r42, r33, r58).
relationships.display_finding: Aligned accuracy stayed within about 0.8–4 points of the original, versus 4–23% accuracy without alignment.

relationships.condition: Cross-architecture linear maps (VGG↔ResNet↔Mixed), Figs 8–9 (text-based, not in rows)
relationships.reason: From the text: off-diagonal OS-LS/MMSE/MLP accuracies are mostly 84–95%, against under 27% without alignment.
relationships.display_finding: Cross-architecture aligned accuracies were mostly 84–95%, versus under 27% without alignment.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 cells with larger linear-map losses
relationships.reason: MMSE drops 5.1 points on ResNet Hyperp (r38) and LS drops 4.6 points on Mixed Hyperp (r57). The loss depends on the estimator choice.
relationships.display_finding: MMSE lost 5.1 accuracy points on ResNet Hyperp, while least squares lost 4.6 points on Mixed Hyperp.

relationships.condition: On-device relative representations: SVHN for all architectures; VGG and ResNet on CIFAR-10
relationships.reason: Accuracy is within about 1–4 points of the original (r05, r10, r25, r30, r45, r50, r15, r20, r35, r40).
relationships.display_finding: On-device relative representations kept accuracy within about 1–4 points of the original.

relationships.condition: On-device relative representations: Mixed architecture on CIFAR-10, and cross-architecture on CIFAR-10 (Fig 10c–d, text-based)
relationships.reason: Mixed drops about 10–11 points (r55, r60). Per Fig 10, cross-architecture CIFAR-10 entries fall to about 69–78% in some pairs.
relationships.display_finding: Mixed-architecture relative representations lost approximately 10–11 accuracy points, and some cross-architecture pairs achieved only approximately 69–78% accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Server-based LS, MMSE, and single-layer MLP alignment across the reported VGG-based, ResNet-based, and mixed aggregates on SVHN and CIFAR-10
reader_labels.reason: Aligned cross-model accuracies are generally close to the stated original-model references, whereas the no-alignment controls are very low; see rows r01-r04, r06-r09, r11-r14, r16-r19, r21-r24, r26-r29, r31-r34, r36-r39, r41-r44, r46-r49, r51-r54, and r56-r59.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: On-device relative-representation alignment for VGG-based and ResNet-based systems, and mixed systems on SVHN
reader_labels.reason: The reported accuracy is close to the original reference in these conditions; see rows r05, r10, r15, r20, r25, r30, and r45, r50.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Accuracy is substantially below the original reference for both training variations; see rows r55 and r60.
